input: Use Johnson City and Tri-Cities Tennessee summer camp guides (Johnson City Press and local parent sites) to find organizations running summer camps and summer programs for kids and teens. For each organization listed, give the organization's own official URL (search for it), never the listing page.
searches: Johnson City Press summer camp guide 2026 2025
Johnson City Press summer camps guide
Into the Fire Johnson City summer camp 2026

candidates.name: Johnson City Parks and Recreation
candidates.note: 2026 offerings included Jump Start JC, Carver Recreation, nature, sports, STEAM and therapeutic camps.

candidates.name: East Tennessee State University
candidates.note: Renaissance Child summer camps offered hands-on enrichment for children in grades 1–6 in 2026.

candidates.name: Hands On! Discovery Center
candidates.note: 2026 weeklong STEAM camps for ages 5–13 and paleontology camps for ages 6–13 at Gray Fossil Site.

candidates.name: Providence Academy
candidates.note: 2026 community summer camps included athletics, fine arts and discovery, with full-day options.

candidates.name: Coalition for Kids
candidates.note: Free 2026 Summer Bridge program combined academic enrichment, field trips, outdoor play and meals.

candidates.name: Boys & Girls Club of Johnson City/Washington County
candidates.note: 2026 summer program served ages 5–18 who had completed kindergarten, with weekday full-day care.

candidates.name: Into the Fire
candidates.note: 2026 four-day morning art camps included themed projects, crafts and a concluding art show.

candidates.name: Appalachian Christian Camp (Camp ACC)
candidates.note: Grade-based Christian summer camps included younger-child day programs and overnight adventure sessions; 2026 photos documented the season.

candidates.name: Doe River Gorge Ministries
candidates.note: 2026 residential adventure camps and teen leadership programs served students in grades 2–12.

candidates.name: Children's Bible Ministries of East Tennessee
candidates.note: Operated Camp Ta-Pa-Win-Go in 2026, with day camp for ages 5–8 and day or overnight options for ages 8–17.
